DIAGNOSIS READY: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia (HHT).

The clinical picture of frequent epistaxis, mucous membrane bleeding, and petechiae with a normal Complete Blood Count (platelets) and normal Coagulation Panel (PT/aPTT) rules out thrombocytopenia and common coagulation factor deficiencies. Given the persistent mucosal bleeding despite normal platelet count and clotting times, this presentation is most consistent with a vascular disorder such as Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia. REQUEST IMAGES: [Nasal endoscopy or facial/limb physical exam photos showing telangiectasias].
